@magpie-community/agent-aider.readme:
# @magpie-community/agent-aider

[Aider](https://aider.chat) as a magpie agent. magpie has no setup of its own
for Aider; with this plugin it is on magpie's Agents page like the agents
magpie ships with.

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-aider
```

Then pick one of magpie's models in Aider's row. magpie writes into
`~/.aider.conf.yml`:

```yaml
model: openai/deepseek/deepseek-flash   # magpie's model, through litellm's openai/ prefix
openai-api-base: http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1
openai-api-key: magpie-aider            # Aider's own key, so Usage names it
show-model-warnings: false
```

Your comments and other settings stay. Picking Aider's own model again, or
switching it off, puts every key back as it was. Restart Aider after a change:
it reads its settings when it starts.

How agent plugins work: [usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents).

@magpie-community/agent-kimi-desktop.readme:
# Kimi desktop Work agent

Use the ordinary **Kimi desktop application's local Work agent** with a model selected in Magpie. This is not Kimi Code CLI, a Kimi subscription provider, or a way to spend Kimi Work subscription credits in other agents.

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-kimi-desktop
```

Open and sign in to Kimi desktop. On Magpie's Agents page select **Kimi**, pick a model, and connect. The adapter waits for the local Work runtime to be ready and idle, then applies the connection without restarting either application. Use Kimi's **Work** page. Chat and cloud Claw are outside its scope. The standard Kimi model menu continues to use the model selected in Magpie; this package does not modify Kimi's application resources or install a custom model-menu patch.

Disconnect Kimi in Magpie to restore its original model service address. Existing conversations, login credentials, unrelated settings, and native model entries are preserved.

## Library: instructions, MCP and skills

Version 0.1.1 registers ordinary **Kimi** as a target on all three Library pages. This is separate from **Kimi Code**. Existing assignments stay unchanged; select Kimi on the resources you want to share.

- Shared instructions are written by Magpie to `~/.config/magpie-kimi/AGENTS.md`. While connected, the adapter reads this file before each inference and inserts one separate system message, preserving Kimi's original prompts, tool calls and history. Changes also apply to existing Work conversations on their next request. Removing the assignment removes Magpie's managed block; other text in that file remains the user's own instructions. An unreadable/invalid file fails with `instructions_unavailable` rather than silently omitting active rules. These instructions do not apply when disconnected, to Chat, or to cloud Claw.
- MCP points through `~/.config/magpie-kimi/library-native/mcp.json` to ordinary Kimi's `daimon-share/daimon/runtime/kimi-code/home/mcp.json`. The format is Kimi's `mcpServers` object. Existing server entries are retained by Magpie's normal Library merge; new conversations load changed MCP settings. Existing conversations can use Kimi's own reconnect controls.
- Skills point through `~/.config/magpie-kimi/library-skills` to ordinary Kimi's `daimon-share/daimon/skills`. This exposes existing native skills as well as Library assignments. Bundled/user skills are not deleted or replaced by the adapter. Conflicts use Magpie's normal keep-own/use-library choice. Start a new Work conversation to load changed skills.

The two directory links are Windows junctions or macOS directory symlinks; no administrator authorization or app modification is needed. An existing different object at either link path is left intact and reports `library_path_conflict`. Resource files remain in Kimi when the model bridge disconnects. The adapter does not enable all resources or change another agent's assignments.

The Work provider carries an agent's messages unchanged; a provider is not a separate instruction target. Give shared instructions to the agent making the request. Using Kimi Work in Codex therefore uses Codex's instructions, while ordinary Kimi uses the Kimi assignment above.

## How it works

The import-free `kimi-desktop.agent.js` registers the agent using Magpie's agent interface. The Bun entry `index.mjs` is also necessary: Kimi's actual configuration belongs to its running local runtime, so changing a file alone does not reliably apply a model. It runs a loopback adapter and uses Kimi's authenticated local control API to reload the selected model.

Inference goes to Magpie using Magpie's agent credential. Kimi's web search/fetch tools continue through Kimi's original `agent-gw.kimi.com` service with Kimi's own credential. Kimi login credentials are never forwarded to Magpie or a third-party model provider. Requests to unknown paths and requests without Kimi authentication are rejected; no system proxy, certificate or firewall settings are changed.

The adapter does not reload a busy Work runtime. If Kimi independently changes its service configuration while connected, adaptation pauses instead of repeatedly overwriting it; disconnect and reconnect in Magpie to retry.

## Local files and compatibility

- `~/.config/magpie-kimi/connection.json`: Magpie's selected model and connection.
- `~/.config/magpie-kimi/status.json`: fixed status categories, without credentials.
- `~/.config/magpie-kimi/adapter-state.json`: original service address and connection ownership; no Kimi login credentials.
- `~/.config/magpie-kimi/before-menu-models.json`: one snapshot of the original model list/current choice, removed after a clean disconnect. No full configuration or credential backup is written.
- Kimi configuration: `kimi-desktop/daimon-share/daimon/config.json` under the platform's application-support directory.

Verified with Windows 11, Kimi 3.2.17.10 and official Magpie 0.1.1275, including an actual Work request through Magpie. The [macOS record](COMPATIBILITY.md) verifies real control methods, connect/disconnect restoration and a real streamed bridge request on macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Kimi 3.2.17 build 3.2.17.4 and official Magpie 0.1.1276. That request was initiated by an HTTP test client; a macOS desktop UI-submitted Work turn remains unverified. The supported runtime has provider `daimon-kimi-code` with original service `https://agent-gw.kimi.com/coding/v1`; other layouts stop with `unsupported_kimi_config`.

The private control API is undocumented. Before connecting, the adapter probes `models.current`; a refused/missing method stops connection without changing the service address. A failed `conversations.setModel` rolls back that address. Failures of `conversations.getKimiModelList` or `conversations.updateKimiModelList` report `catalog_sync_failed` and preserve the existing catalog rather than inventing a different protocol. In that case the selected-model bridge may remain connected; disconnect it to return to Kimi's service. No vendor app files are patched, and no automatic upgrade to an unknown protocol is attempted.

No Kimi binaries, personal configuration, prompts, account identifiers or credentials are included. There are no runtime dependencies. Tests use isolated temporary directories and synthetic credentials.

```sh
bun test packages/kimi-desktop/kimi-desktop.test.mjs
```

The model catalog is fetched from Magpie's `/v1/models` with this agent's credential and registered User-Agent. Magpie owns its visibility, picked/hidden models, disables and ordering. The adapter never opens Magpie's `providers.json` or `settings.json`. It rechecks the gateway catalog before every inference; removed selections are refused even during a running turn, and an unavailable catalog returns a fixed error instead of falling back to an unrestricted list. This package includes no Electron injection hook or model-menu patch. The icon is Kimi's desktop application icon.

## Shutdown and manual recovery

The shared plugin host owns process shutdown. This plugin installs no SIGTERM/SIGINT handler and never calls `process.exit`. On the host's normal exit event it synchronously restores the original address if the current address is still its own; restart Kimi to reload its runtime. An explicit disconnect while both apps are running additionally restores model selection/list through the control API.

A forced kill, power loss or a broken private API can leave Kimi pointing at an inactive loopback bridge. To recover without starting Magpie:

1. Close Kimi normally. In `~/.config/magpie-kimi/connection.json`, set `enabled` to `false` so the adapter does not reconnect when Magpie next starts.
2. Open Kimi's `config.json` at the application-support path above. Only if `model.providers["daimon-kimi-code"].baseUrl` equals `bridgeURL` in `adapter-state.json`, change that one field to the same state's `originalBase` (normally `https://agent-gw.kimi.com/coding/v1`). Leave `credentials` and all unrelated fields untouched; do not replace the whole document from an old backup.
3. If `model.current` starts with `magpie-local-`, set it to `current` from `before-menu-models.json` if that alias still exists in `model.models`; otherwise choose an existing native `daimon-kimi-code` alias, such as `k3-agent` or `k2d8-preview`. Remove only `model.models` keys beginning with `magpie-local-` if present. Reopen Kimi; it refreshes its native model catalog.

Older experimental packages created full `backups/before-connect-*.json` copies, which can contain Kimi credentials. This package creates no such files and does not silently delete existing user backups. After recovery, users can remove those older copies locally. Do not upload them in an issue or PR.

# @magpie-community/agent-type4me

[Type4Me](https://github.com/joewongjc/type4me), a macOS voice input app, as a
magpie agent. With this plugin Type4Me is on magpie's Agents page like the
agents magpie ships with: pick one of magpie's models for its LLM
post-processing in Type4Me's row.

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/agent-type4me
```

Until it is on npm, install it from GitHub:

```sh
magpie plugin add github:kchen0x/magpie-agent-type4me
```

Then pick one of magpie's models in Type4Me's row, or
`magpie type4me magpie/deepseek/deepseek-flash`. magpie writes into
`~/Library/Application Support/Type4Me/magpie-agent.json`:

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash",
  "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
  "apiKey": "magpie-…"
}
```

In Type4Me, choose **Magpie (Local Gateway)** under Settings › Models and set
it as the default. Type4Me reads the file before each dictation, so a new model
takes effect on the next one, with no restart.

- Type4Me and Type4Me Dev share that folder: one plugin covers both.
- Picking a model in Type4Me's own settings changes it in magpie too (Type4Me
  runs `magpie type4me magpie/<model>`). Type4Me never changes `baseURL` or
  `apiKey`.
- Switching Type4Me off in magpie removes the three keys; Type4Me then talks to
  magpie directly, with the model picked in Type4Me.

Type4Me works with magpie without this plugin too, listing magpie's models
itself. The plugin adds Type4Me to magpie's Agents page, menu bar and profiles.

How agent plugins work: [usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins#agents).

## Develop

The source lives at [kchen0x/magpie-agent-type4me](https://github.com/kchen0x/magpie-agent-type4me)
and is copied to `packages/type4me` in
[magpie-community/plugins](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins).

```sh
bun test                                # what connect returns
magpie plugin add ./type4me.agent.js    # try it on your own magpie
```

`agent.config` must match `MagpieAgentFile.defaultURL` in Type4Me.

@magpie-community/middleware-antigravity.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-antigravity-cloak

Claude Code and Claude Desktop on an Antigravity account, as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware.

Antigravity answers a request whose system prompt reads as Claude Code's or the Claude Agent SDK's (which Claude Desktop's chats use) with `429 Resource has been exhausted`, however much quota is left. magpie shows it as a 400 that says so. Tried with a real account, Antigravity matches two pieces of the prompt:

- Claude Code's billing line, `x-anthropic-billing-header: …`;
- `You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK`.

The same prompt goes through when each has a zero-width space (U+200B) inside it. This middleware puts one after the first letter of `x-anthropic-billing-header` and `Claude Agent SDK`, in the system prompt only, and only in what an Antigravity account is sent. Every other provider, a Claude subscription above all, gets the prompt as the agent wrote it, even in a routing group that tries Antigravity first. The model reads the words as before.

It needs a magpie with the `onProvider` hook (v0.1.1283 or later): an older magpie loads it and never calls it, so requests go as they came.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-antigravity-cloak`.

## Before you turn it on

- This changes what Google is sent so that a request it means to refuse isn't refused. It may be against Antigravity's terms, and Google can ban the account for it. Use it on an account you can afford to lose.
- Google can change what it matches at any time. Then the refusal comes back, and magpie may no longer recognise it as this refusal: it can read as a real quota running out and rest the account. If that happens, add the new words to `extraWords`, or turn the plugin off.

## Options

```json
{ "extraWords": [], "accounts": ["antigravity"], "off": false }
```

- `extraWords`: more words to break the same way, matched whatever their case.
- `accounts`: the subscriptions it acts on, by kind. `antigravity` is the default.
- `off`: leave every request as it came.

中文：Antigravity 看到 Claude Code / Claude Agent SDK 的系统提示词会回一个假的 429。这个中间件只在发给 Antigravity 账号的请求里，往 `x-anthropic-billing-header` 和 `Claude Agent SDK` 里插一个零宽空格，其他供应商（尤其是 Claude 订阅）收到的提示词不变。这样做可能违反 Antigravity 的条款，账号有被封的风险，请只用在可以承受损失的账号上。需要 magpie v0.1.1283 或更新版本。

After [hexiaolv/magpie-antigravity-cloak](https://github.com/hexiaolv/magpie-antigravity-cloak) (MIT), which breaks a longer list of words in every request, whatever provider it goes to.

@magpie-community/middleware-block-patte.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-block-patterns

Rejects requests that contain text you list, as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. A request with one of your words or patterns in it is turned away with a 400 before it reaches a model; everything else is sent on untouched.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-block-patterns`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options block-patterns '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "words": ["project-codename"],
  "patterns": ["\\b\\d{3}-\\d{4}\\b"],
  "system": true,
  "message": "" }
```

- **`words`.** Plain substrings, matched anywhere in the text, ignoring case.
- **`patterns`.** Regular expressions, also matched ignoring case.
- **`system`.** `true` (the default) reads the system prompt as well as the user's turns, so a word in either turns the request away. `false` leaves every system prompt out and reads the user's turns alone. Where each API keeps its system prompt is listed under "What it reads".
- **`message`.** The error text to use in place of the default one.

## What it reads

Every content shape an agent sends, in all four APIs magpie serves: plain string content, `text` and `input_text` blocks, Responses `input` items, and Gemini `parts`. Anthropic, Chat Completions, Responses and Gemini are all covered.

Every user turn is read, not only the last one, so a word earlier in the conversation is caught. System prompts are read too, unless you set `system` to `false`. Each API keeps its system prompt in its own place, and all of them are read:

| API | Read when `system` is true |
|---|---|
| Anthropic | the top-level `system` field, as a string or as text blocks, and any `system` / `developer` message |
| Chat Completions | any `system` / `developer` message |
| Responses | `instructions`, and any `system` / `developer` input item |
| Gemini | `systemInstruction` and `system_instruction`, as a string or as a `{ parts }` object |

Tool calls, tool arguments, tool results and Gemini thought parts are never read, so a file an agent reads that contains a word doesn't stop it, and a word the model said back doesn't either.

## If a pattern does not compile

A `patterns` entry that is not a valid regular expression is ignored, and the rest of your options still work. Nothing is thrown: a typo in one entry cannot turn away every request the gateway sees. Fix the pattern in **Plugins › Installed › Options** — the entries that failed are not reported, so check the spelling if a word you listed seems to be passing through.

## What it is not

This is literal matching, not a safety classifier. It does not understand what a request means, and it does not judge whether anything is harmful. A synonym, a paraphrase, a misspelling or a word split by formatting passes it. Don't rely on it as a real guardrail against a determined prompt: use it to keep listed text — an internal codename, a customer's name, an unreleased feature — out of what your gateway sends.

## Word Guard vs this

Both match a list of words and regular expressions, and both can turn a request away, so it is worth saying which to install.

- **Word Guard** can mask a match and send the request on, and can mask matches in the replies as well. It reads only the last user message by default, and never reads a system prompt.
- **This one** only turns requests away — there is no mask and it never reads replies. In exchange it reads every user turn and every system prompt, wherever the API keeps it.

Install this one when you want a listed word to be an error rather than something silently rewritten, and when a system prompt is part of what you want to keep off the wire. Install Word Guard when you would rather the request go through with the word blanked out. They can be installed together.

magpie already redacts secrets (API keys and tokens) before a request leaves your computer, and puts them back in the reply. Neither package is needed for that.

中文：按你列出的词与正则拒绝请求（纯字面匹配，不是安全分类器），可选择是否读取 system 提示词。

@magpie-community/middleware-codex-histo.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-codex-history

**Magpie 原生历史过滤插件 / Native history compatibility middleware**

缓解 Codex 切换供应商、账号或上游资源后，旧会话出现密文验证失败、部分历史 item ID 不属于当前资源的问题。只处理发出的 Responses 请求，不修改原会话文件或 Codex `base_url`。

**插件只提供历史过滤，不包含 ModelTrace、降智检测或模型保护。** 无独立后台服务、管理端口、运行时依赖或额外模型请求。规则默认全部关闭，在 Magpie 自带的插件 Options 中按供应商设置。

## 安装

在 Magpie 的 **Plugins → Discover → Gateway middleware** 中安装 **Codex History Filter**，或使用命令行：

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-codex-history
```

社区版本只发布历史过滤中间件；模型工作台单独本地维护，不包含在本包中。无需启动 Codex Filter Manager，不要同时启用两份过滤插件。需要支持 gateway middleware 的 Magpie；本包已在 0.1.1265 的隔离实例中验证，其他版本需核对插件加载状态。

## 设置

打开 **Plugins → Installed → 本插件 → Options**，保存以下示例，替换 `demo` 和 `backup` 为你实际使用的 Magpie 供应商 ID：

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "magpie:demo": {
      "historyFilter": true,
      "preserveEncryptedInclude": true
    },
    "magpie:backup": {
      "historyFilter": false,
      "preserveEncryptedInclude": true
    }
  },
  "aliases": {}
}
```

- 请求模型为 `demo/gpt-6-astra` 时，使用 `magpie:demo` 的规则；ID 是模型前缀，不是供应商显示名称。
- `historyFilter: true` 开启过滤；`false`、删除该规则或空配置均为直通。不同会话按各自请求独立处理，可同时过滤多个供应商。
- `preserveEncryptedInclude: true` 保留客户端对**新响应**中 `reasoning.encrypted_content` 的请求，推荐开启。它不会保留**旧历史**中的密文。省略或设置为 `false` 会移除这一 include 值，不影响其他 include 项。
- 供应商改名后，旧会话可能仍发送旧前缀；可设置 `"aliases": {"old-demo": "demo"}`。别名只用于选择过滤规则，不改写请求模型，也不替代 Magpie 自己的路由别名。
- 无 `供应商/模型` 前缀或非 Responses 协议的请求保持原样。未配置的供应商不会被自动过滤。

保存 Options 后，Magpie 在后续请求加载规则。无需另开网页或重启 Codex；是否成功加载以 Magpie 插件页的错误与调用统计为准。

## 原理与边界

开启后，插件移除旧 reasoning 条目、明确标记的加密内容，以及可独立携带内容的消息和工具条目中的可选服务器 ID；设置 `store: false`。保留正文、工具参数、结果、`call_id` 配对、文件引用及普通业务 ID，不改变请求模型或推理强度。

**v0.1.1：历史搜索兼容修复。** 原生 `web_search_call` 可能依赖已删除的 reasoning，导致上游提示 `was provided without its required reasoning item`。开启过滤后，历史搜索条目转为带标记的助手文字，保留已记录的动作、查询、状态和来源数据，去除服务器条目 ID 与内部回合元数据；后续结论、引用及普通工具调用配对保持原样。不重新搜索、不补造未记录的结果。该处理适用于携带明文历史的普通对话和文字总结，不解密压缩历史。

`previous_response_id`、`conversation`、`item_reference`、加密压缩历史和 `/responses/compact` 无法安全跨资源迁移时，会明确拒绝，提示整理文字摘要后新建会话，不会静默丢弃这些上下文。

- 不能解密旧密文、迁移所有服务器资源引用，或保证消除全部 Azure 历史错误。移除内部推理状态也可能影响长任务连续性。
- Magpie 请求钩子限时 250 毫秒；加载失败、异常或超时可能按 Magpie 的机制放行原请求。插件不是强制安全边界。
- 只覆盖进入 Magpie agent middleware 的 Responses 请求；Magpie 自身的标题、分类器等内部请求不经过此钩子。WebSocket、Chat Completions、Lite HTTP 标头修改不在本插件范围内。
- 规则按进入钩子时的模型前缀选择。自动路由组、fallback、其他插件随后改写路由时，不保证规则对应最终上游。
- 不采集或保存凭据、请求正文，不执行检测、重试或模型调用。上游正常请求仍按上游规则计费。

## 停用、升级与旧版迁移

在 Magpie 插件页关闭本插件即可停止全部过滤；删除某条供应商规则只停用该供应商。卸载也在 Magpie 中完成，不需要恢复 `base_url`。通过本地路径安装时，移动或删除目录前先卸载旧插件。

若此前使用 Codex Filter Manager v1.0.5 自动安装的本地 `magpie-plugin`，先在旧管理页关闭该供应商的自动保护（若有旧设置），停止旧管理服务，再在 Magpie 中停用或卸载旧的本地历史插件，最后安装本插件并复制所需历史规则。原有规则的 `stripResponsesLiteHeader` 会被忽略，可删除。不要同时启用两份历史过滤插件。

社区版本合并并完成 dist 发布后，可在 Magpie 插件页更新；现有 Options 无需改写，更新前可自行备份。不要上传 Magpie 的 `plugins.json`，它可能包含其他插件的私有设置。本插件不直接读写该文件，规则由宿主通过 Options 传入。

## English

Opt-in Magpie gateway middleware for Codex Responses history after switching providers or accounts. It strips old reasoning/encrypted items and optional server IDs from portable history, preserving readable content and tool-call pairing. **History filtering only: no model detector, guard, background server, credentials or extra upstream calls.**

Install from **Plugins → Discover → Gateway middleware**, or run `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-codex-history`. In the plugin's **Options**, configure `providers["magpie:<provider-id>"]` as shown above. Every provider defaults to passthrough. The request's `provider/model` prefix selects its rule; requests from different sessions remain independent. `aliases` maps an old prefix to a rule ID only. `preserveEncryptedInclude: true` keeps requests for new encrypted response content while still removing historical ciphertext.

Unsafe server-only references and encrypted compaction are rejected explicitly. Magpie may fail open on plugin errors/timeouts, and downstream route changes are outside the plugin's control. Disable or remove it in Magpie; it never edits Codex configuration.

Version 0.1.1 converts historical native `web_search_call` items to labeled assistant text after removing old reasoning. Recorded actions, queries, status and sources remain available; native item IDs and internal turn metadata are removed. Subsequent answers and ordinary tool-call pairs remain intact. No searches are rerun, absent results are not reconstructed, and encrypted compaction is not decrypted. The community package contains only the middleware; the optional model workbench is maintained separately for local use.

## 开发与来源

```sh
bun test packages/codex-history
```

测试只使用本地虚构数据，不调用模型。核心代码来自 [Codex Filter Manager v1.0.5](https://github.com/unisong/codex-filter-manager/tree/v1.0.5)，来源和 SHA-256 记录于 [PROVENANCE.json](PROVENANCE.json)。为匹配社区 middleware 包格式，将共用算法与请求钩子合并为单个无 import 文件。

@magpie-community/middleware-model-map.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-model-map

New API's **模型重定向** (a channel's `model_mapping`) as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. The model an agent asks for is sent upstream as another model. Replies then name the model the agent asked for, so an agent that reads its model's name back (Claude Code does, to size its context window) sees the name it asked for.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-model-map`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options model-map '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "mapping": {
    "fast": "deepseek-chat",
    "/^claude-(.*)$/": "glm-$1"
} }
```

- **Mapping.** A name maps to its target. Names chain (`a → b → c`) until there is nothing more to map, and a cycle stops before it repeats.
- **Patterns.** A key written `/like this/` is a regular expression, and its target can use `$1` for the first group.
- **Flat form.** New API's flat form, `{"fast": "deepseek-chat"}`, works as well.
- **`keep_upstream_name`.** Set it to `true` to leave the upstream model's name in replies.

The target has to be a model magpie can route: a model of one of your providers, or one of magpie's own ids (`deepseek/deepseek-chat`, for example).

**Gemini.** A Gemini request names its model in the URL; magpie moves it into the body before the middleware runs, so it is mapped like any other API, and the reply's `modelVersion` names the model asked for again.

中文：New API 的「模型重定向」，作为 magpie 网关中间件。回复里的模型名会还原成 agent 请求时用的名字。

@magpie-community/middleware-param-overr.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-param-override

New API's **参数覆盖** (a channel's `param_override`) as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. It sets, deletes, moves and rewrites any field of the requests agents send through magpie, whichever provider serves them. The options are New API's JSON as it is, so you can paste a `param_override` from New API unchanged.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-param-override`. Then set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options param-override '<json>'`.

## Options

There are two forms, as in New API:

```json
{ "temperature": 0.2, "max_tokens": 8000 }
```

Each key is set on the body as it is.

```json
{ "operations": [
  { "path": "max_tokens", "mode": "set", "value": 32000,
    "conditions": [{ "path": "max_tokens", "mode": "gt", "value": 32000 }] },
  { "path": "temperature", "mode": "delete",
    "conditions": [{ "path": "model", "mode": "contains", "value": "reasoner" }] },
  { "mode": "return_error", "value": { "message": "opus is not allowed here", "status_code": 403 },
    "conditions": [{ "path": "model", "mode": "contains", "value": "opus" }] }
] }
```

The operations run in order. Keys set beside `operations` are applied first.

| Field | |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | A gjson path: `a.b.0`. `messages.-1` counts from the end, `tools.*.name` matches every item, and `\.` is a dot inside a key. |
| `mode` | `set` (`keep_origin`: only when missing), `delete`, `move` / `copy` (`from`, `to`), `prepend` / `append` (arrays joined, strings joined, objects merged; `keep_origin` keeps keys already there), `trim_prefix`, `trim_suffix`, `ensure_prefix`, `ensure_suffix`, `trim_space`, `to_lower`, `to_upper`, `replace` / `regex_replace` (`from`, `to`; Go's `${1}` works), `return_error`, `prune_objects` |
| `value` | What to set, join or trim. For `return_error`, a message or `{message, status_code}`; the agent gets the error in its own API's shape. For `prune_objects`, a `type` or `{type, where, conditions, logic, recursive}`. |
| `conditions` | `[{path, mode, value, invert, pass_missing_key}]`, where `mode` is `full`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `contains`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt` or `lte`. A path is looked up in the body first, then in the request: `model`, `request_path`, `protocol` (`anthropic`, `chat`, `responses`, `gemini`), `agent`, `stream`. |
| `logic` | `OR` (New API's default) or `AND`. |

Some of New API's modes have nothing to act on here and are left out: the header modes (`set_header`, `pass_headers`…), `sync_fields`, and conditions on retries, users and groups. The middleware sees only the body.

Unlike New API, an operation that can't apply is skipped (a `move` from a missing path, `trim_prefix` on a number) and the request goes on. If the middleware itself fails, magpie sends the request as it came.

## Recipes

- Cap `max_tokens` for a provider with a lower limit: the first example above.
- Drop a parameter a provider refuses: `{"path": "tools.*.input_examples", "mode": "delete"}`.
- Strip a vendor prefix from model names: `{"path": "model", "mode": "trim_prefix", "value": "openai/"}`.
- Keep an agent off a model: `return_error` with a `model` condition.
- Remove old thinking blocks: `{"path": "messages", "mode": "prune_objects", "value": "thinking"}`.

中文：New API 的「参数覆盖」，作为 magpie 网关中间件。配置是 New API 的同一份 JSON，可以原样粘贴过来。

@magpie-community/middleware-reserve.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-reserve

Two routings for [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) that keep something in reserve. Pick one for a provider's accounts or keys, or for a routing group's members, and magpie's gateway tries them in the order it gives.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-reserve`. While it is on, every routing picker offers `reserve/ceiling` and `reserve/accounts-first`. From the command line, a group takes one with:

```sh
magpie group set <id> routing=reserve/ceiling
```

## Routings

**`reserve/ceiling`** fills the accounts in the order listed, but keeps the last share of each one's allowance.

- The first account takes requests until it has used `ceiling` percent of its allowance, then the next one takes over.
- Once every account is past the ceiling, the least used goes first.
- A seat whose allowance isn't known (an API key, or an account not read yet) counts as below the ceiling.
- A seat resting after a failure goes last.

Use it to keep, say, a fifth of your main account's week for when you're at its own app, while the gateway uses the rest.

**`reserve/accounts-first`** puts subscriptions before API keys, so what you have paid for already goes first. A key that bills by the token is used only when no account can take the request.

- Accounts go least used first.
- Keys go by their weight, highest first, then by what they were sent lately.
- Seats resting after a failure go last.

## Options

```json
{ "ceiling": 80 }
```

`ceiling` is the percent of an account's allowance past which `reserve/ceiling` moves on, from 1 to 100. It is 80 when none is set. Set it under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options reserve '{"ceiling": 70}'`.

## Test

`strategies.json` holds the cases: seats in, the order wanted out. `reserve.test.mjs` runs them with `checkStrategies()` from `scripts/middleware.mjs`, and checks that each answer is a permutation of the seats.

```sh
bun test packages/reserve
```

中文：两种为账号留余量的路由。`reserve/ceiling` 按列出的顺序使用账号，每个账号用到额度的 `ceiling`%（默认 80）就换下一个，全部超过后用得最少的优先；`reserve/accounts-first` 订阅账号优先于按量计费的 API key，key 按权重排序。休息中的总是排最后。

@magpie-community/middleware-system-prom.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-system-prompt

New API's **系统提示词** (a channel's `system_prompt` and its override switch) as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. It gives the requests agents send a system prompt of yours, in each API's own place for one:

| API | Where the prompt goes |
| --- | --- |
| Anthropic | `system` |
| Chat | the first `system` or `developer` message |
| Responses | `instructions` |
| Gemini | `systemInstruction` |

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-system-prompt`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options system-prompt '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "system_prompt": "Reply in the language the user writes in.",
  "override": true, "position": "append",
  "agents": ["claude"], "models": ["deepseek"] }
```

- **No system prompt yet.** A request without one gets yours.
- **`override`.** A request that has its own prompt keeps it unchanged, unless `override` is `true`. Then yours goes in as well, placed by `position`:
  - `"append"` (the default) puts yours after it. Agents cache their own prompt, so adding after it keeps that cache.
  - `"prepend"` puts yours before it, as New API does. This makes the provider read the whole prompt again on every turn.
- **`agents`.** When given, the prompt applies only to these agents, by magpie's agent ids: `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, and so on.
- **`models`.** When given, the prompt applies only to models whose names begin with one of these prefixes.

Codex sends its own model instructions, and changing them can change how its models behave. Use `agents` to leave Codex out if you don't want that.

中文：New API 的「系统提示词」，作为 magpie 网关中间件。默认把你的提示词加在 agent 自己的提示词之后，这样不会破坏提示缓存。

# @magpie-community/middleware-think-tags

A model's thinking, where its reply's text is, as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. It either takes thinking out of the text, or puts it in (New API's `thinking_to_content`).

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-think-tags`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options think-tags '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "mode": "strip" }
```

**`strip`** (the default). Some models (open reasoning models served by vLLM, Ollama and many relays) write their thinking into the reply as `<think>…</think>`. This mode takes that block out, so an agent doesn't keep it in its history and send it back every turn.

- Only a block at the start of the text is taken out. A `<think>` the model writes later, in code for example, stays.
- A `</think>` inside the block in Markdown code (`` `</think>` ``, or a fenced block) is part of the thinking, an example written out, not its end.
- A tag split across streamed chunks is still found.
- It works on Anthropic, Chat and Responses replies, streamed or whole.

**`to_content`**. A Chat reply's `reasoning_content` (or `reasoning`) is put into its text as `<think>…</think>`, for a client that shows only the text.

- This mode works on Chat replies only. An Anthropic thinking block carries a signature, and turned into text it would fail the next turn.
- It changes what the agent keeps and sends back, so it suits a chat client better than a coding agent.

中文：`strip` 去掉回复开头模型写出的 `<think>…</think>`；`to_content` 把 Chat 回复的 reasoning_content 放进正文（New API 的 thinking_to_content）。

@magpie-community/middleware-word-guard.readme:
# @magpie-community/middleware-word-guard

New API's **敏感词过滤** as [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) gateway middleware. It keeps the words and patterns you list out of what agents send: a request with one is turned away, or has the word masked. It can mask them in replies too.

Install it from magpie's **Plugins › Discover**, or with `magpie plugin add @magpie-community/middleware-word-guard`. Set its options under **Plugins › Installed › Options**, or with `magpie plugin options word-guard '<json>'`.

## Options

```json
{ "words": ["project-codename"],
  "patterns": ["\\b\\d{3}-\\d{4}\\b"],
  "action": "reject",
  "check": "last" }
```

- **`words`.** Words matched anywhere in the text, ignoring case.
- **`patterns`.** Regular expressions, also matched ignoring case.
- **`action`.** `reject` (the default) turns the request away with a 400 that names the word, in the agent's API's error shape. `mask` replaces each match with `mask` (default `***`) and sends the request on.
- **`check`.** `last` (the default) reads only the last user message that has text, which is the turn being sent. That is what New API reads. `all` reads every user message, so a word earlier in the conversation keeps turning requests away.
- **`replies`.** Set it to `true` to mask matches in the text that comes back as well, in every API magpie serves — Anthropic, Chat, Responses and Gemini, streamed or whole. A word split across two streamed events isn't caught.
- **`message`.** The error text to use in place of the default one.

The middleware reads only the user's own text. It doesn't read tool results, tool calls or the system prompt, so a file an agent reads that contains the word doesn't stop it.

If you want a listed word to be a 400 rather than something masked, and you also want every earlier user turn and the system prompt read, that is [block-patterns](../block-patterns). It never masks and never reads replies, so the two can be installed together.

magpie already redacts secrets (API keys and tokens) before a request leaves your computer, and puts them back in the reply. You don't need this middleware for secrets.

中文：New API 的「敏感词过滤」，作为 magpie 网关中间件。只检查用户自己写的文字，可拒绝请求或替换成 `***`，也可以替换回复里的词。

# @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) / [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) provider 插件：**AutoClaw（智谱澳龙 / OpenClaw 云端账号体系）**。

一个包注册两个供应商，按账号所在地分开登录、分开记额度：

| 供应商 id | 登录方式 | 上游 host | 模型引用 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autoclaw` | Google / z.ai 网页 OAuth | `autoglm-api.autoglm.ai` | `autoclaw/zai_auto` 等 |
| `autoclaw-cn` | 手机验证码（+86） | `autoglm-api.zhipuai.cn` | `autoclaw-cn/zai_auto` 等 |

两个供应商都支持 magpie 的多账号、故障切换、token 自动轮换与积分余额显示。实测可用的 4 个在线模型为带前缀的 routeModelId（`zai_` 智谱 / `zaicoding_` coding plan）：

- `zai_auto` / `zai_auto-fast`（自动路由，支持 reasoning variants：low / high / max）
- `zai_glm-5.3-flash`（极速推理，支持 reasoning variants）
- `zaicoding_glm-5.3`（GLM-5.3 编程专项，支持 reasoning variants）

> 注：旧版中的 `zai_glm-5-turbo` 以及豆包 DeepSeek 映射 `tdpsk_deepseek-v4-flash-202605`、`tdpsk_deepseek-v4-pro-202606` 已被上游下线（调用均返回 `400 非法模型`），本版本已从模型列表中移除。

## 安装

```sh
magpie plugin add @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth
magpie plugin login autoclaw                   # Google / z.ai 网页登录
magpie plugin login autoclaw-cn                # 手机验证码
magpie provider test autoclaw zai_auto
magpie quota                                   # 积分余额
```

OpenCode 同样可加载（`opencode auth login`）。登录信息保存在 magpie 的 `plugin-auth.json`（600 权限）/ OpenCode 的 `auth.json`。

## 直连说明（不经本地网关）

插件**直连上游云 API**，登录/对话/刷新/积分全部自行完成：

- 对话走 `POST {host}/autoclaw-proxy/proxy/autoclaw/v1/chat/completions`（`X-Authorization` 鉴权）；
- token 过期前自动轮换（refresh token 一次一换，`auth.refresh` 钩子交给 magpie 串行化，不会双花）；
- 积分余额通过 `auth.usage` 显示（纯积分制，无总量上限，`aside` 窗口展示余额）；
- **国际版登录是完整本地实现**：插件在 127.0.0.1 上取官方 TokenServer 端口池中的一个端口
  （18432/19654/19723/53699，OAuth client 回调白名单；被占自动顺延）起临时服务器，内嵌引导页完成
  阿里滑块验证（`AliyunCaptcha` SDK，`ali_captcha_verify_param` 回执）→ 获取授权页 →
  自动跳转 Google/z.ai → 回调自动捕获 code，全程浏览器完成、无需粘贴；登录结束服务器即关
  （未完成时 10 分钟后自动关闭释放端口）。回调 code 必须匹配授权页下发的 `state`，其余一律拒收
  （防伪造回调劫持登录）；本地服务器的写接口仅接受 127.0.0.1/localhost 来源。

## 每日签到

两种方式，推荐用**原生签到**：

**① magpie 原生签到（magpie ≥ v0.1.1083，推荐）**：插件实现 `auth.checkin` 钩子，走 magpie 统一调度——Settings → Usage → Plugins 里每个供应商有 **Daily check-in** 开关（默认关），打开后每天每账号自动签一次（北京时间；启动 2 分钟后首查、每 30 分钟轮询，失败 30 分钟后重试），账户 Usage 卡片显示签到结果，也可 **Check in now** 手动签。

**② 旧链路自动补签（默认关）**：查额度（`magpie quota`、GUI 刷新）与 token 刷新时发现未签就补签（服务端幂等，本地按天去重、失败按小时重试）。旧版 magpie / OpenCode 宿主或偏好该行为的用户开启 `signinOnUsage`。

`magpie quota` 的额度窗口里始终显示**每日签到**状态行（今日已签 ✓ / 今日未签 +N）。

旧链路的开关有**两个通道**（插件 options 优先，配置文件兜底；原生签到开关只在 GUI 的 Settings 里）：

```sh
# 通道 1：插件 options（magpie CLI）
magpie plugin options @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth '{"signin": false}'        # 关闭自动补签总开关
magpie plugin options @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth '{"signinHour": 8}'        # 只在 8:00–8:59 补签
magpie plugin options @magpie-community/opencode-autoclaw-auth '{"signinOnUsage": true}'  # 开启查额度/刷新自动补签

# 通道 2：配置文件 ~/.config/magpie/autoclaw.json（保存即生效，热读取）
cat > ~/.config/magpie/autoclaw.json <<'EOF'
{ "signin": true, "signinHour": null, "signinOnUsage": true }
EOF
```

| 选项 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `signin` | `true` | 旧链路自动补签总开关（不影响原生 checkin） |
| `signinOnUsage` | `false` | 查额度/刷新时自动补签（默认关，交给原生开关） |
| `signinHour` | `null` | 限定补签小时：`8` = 仅当本地时间处于 8:00–8:59 时补签；`null` 不限 |

## 对话网关与请求整形

AutoClaw 对话网关对请求形状有硬性要求，缺任一条都回 `406 Not Acceptable` 且 body 为空：
- **官方 system 前缀**：必须以 `You are AutoClaw. Answer the user directly and concisely.` 开头（插件会自动合并进 caller 已有的 system 消息，无 system 时补一条最小 system）
- **删除 max_tokens**：网关拒收 `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens`，插件会在发送前自动剔除
- **不发送 X-Harness-Type**：上游收到 `X-Harness-Type` 即报 406，已删除该残留请求头
- **改写外部 Harness 身份声明**：上游拦截 system 中包含的外部 agent 身份句（如 `You are Codex`、`You are Claude Code` 等），插件的 `unflag` 会自动将其替换为兼容措辞，避免 406 拦截

国内版 `autoclaw-cn` 走 AutoClaw 2.1.0 managed gateway（`autoglm-acceleration-api.zhipuai.cn`）；国际版 `autoclaw` 走海外直连网关（`autoglm-api.autoglm.ai`）。两者均已通过真实调用与推理验证。

## 已知行为

- 手机号账号只认国内 host（走 managed gateway，401/403 标记登录失效）；z.ai/Google 账号只认国际 host（401/403 自动换侧重试，均拒绝时标记失效）。
- 上游模型白名单随版本变化，模型下线时上游返回 `400 非法模型`（原样透传错误消息）。
- refresh token 与 AutoClaw 桌面端**共用会互踢**（双方都轮换），插件账号请勿同时在桌面端登录。
- 上游偶发改协议时，`CLIENT_VERSION` / 端点路径可能需要随官方客户端更新。

## 免责声明

本包为**非官方**社区插件，与智谱 AI / OpenClaw / AutoClaw 无任何关联。实现基于对官方客户端行为的逆向分析与实测，仅供个人学习研究；使用产生的账号风险由使用者自行承担。上游协议变更可能导致插件随时失效。

### Local sign-in page ownership

The plugin waits for the loopback listener before returning its guide URL. Magpie/OpenCode opens that URL; the callback does not launch a second browser through a shell. Cancelled or expired sessions release their port; begin a new sign-in rather than reusing the old URL.

The guide distinguishes an intentional authorization redirect from the user closing the page. The redirect must keep the loopback callback alive; closing a guide before authorization still cancels it. The guide reports a disconnected or expired session explicitly.

# @magpie-community/opencode-cline-auth

Cline (cline.bot) on your own Cline account: the models Cline's gateway
serves — usage-billed models, ClinePass's and Cline's free models alike.
Provider id: `cline`.

## Signing in

- **Cline device sign-in** — the flow Cline's own client runs: the plugin asks
  WorkOS for a device code and opens the approval page, polls until you
  approve, then trades the WorkOS tokens at Cline's `/api/v1/auth/register`
  for the account's own token pair.
- **Cline API key** — create one at [app.cline.bot → Settings → API Keys](https://app.cline.bot/dashboard/account)
  and paste it. Sent as a plain Bearer key.

The sign-in is kept where OpenCode keeps auth (`auth.json` under the data
directory); magpie keeps plugin sign-ins in its own store
(`~/.config/magpie/plugin-auth.json`).

Refreshing:
- Access tokens are renewed through `/api/v1/auth/refresh`. Cline rotates
  the refresh token and refuses one already spent, so the rotated pair is
  kept in memory beside the store the moment it arrives: a save that fails
  can't leave the next request spending the token that was already spent.
- magpie renews the token ten minutes before it ends, through the plugin's
  `auth.refresh`, once for the account and before its requests, models and
  usage need it; magpie saves the new pair. OpenCode doesn't call that hook:
  there the token is refreshed five minutes before it ends, before a
  request, and the new pair is saved.
- Refreshes are serialized, magpie's renewal included, so two at once can't
  spend one token and lose the other; one that finds the token already
  renewed uses that pair.
- A refresh that fails for a while keeps the token that is still good, as
  Cline's own client does (magpie tries its renewal again shortly); only a
  refresh Cline refuses, or a token that has actually expired, is treated as
  the sign-in gone.

## Requests

Chat completions go to `https://api.cline.bot/api/v1/chat/completions` in
OpenAI's format (streaming included), with `Authorization: Bearer
workos:<access token>` for a signed-in account or the raw API key, and the
full client-identity header set Cline's own clients send (`HTTP-Referer`,
`X-Title`, `User-Agent: Cline/<version>`, `X-CLIENT-TYPE: cline-cli`,
`X-CLIENT-VERSION`, `X-PLATFORM`, `X-PLATFORM-VERSION`, `X-CORE-VERSION`,
`X-IS-MULTIROOT`) — pinned to Cline's current CLI release, which is also
what the free models' gate reads; when Cline ships a new release, move the
pinned numbers in `index.mjs` along. All models use one `X-Task-ID` per
named chat session, derived as a UUID from the session. With no named session
(including magpie's synthetic id from the first user message), no task id
is sent. The session crosses the plugin's hooks in a private header that is
removed before the request goes to Cline. Auth and account requests carry
the same identity. A finished non-streaming answer rides in a
`{"data": …}` envelope the official clients take apart; the plugin takes it
apart too. The model list is read from
`/api/v1/ai/cline/recommended-models` and `/api/v1/ai/cline/models` (neither
needs a sign-in); usage reads `/api/v1/users/me` and the account's `/balance`
(its balance is counted in millionths of a dollar), and ClinePass's 5-hour,
weekly and monthly limits from `/api/v1/users/me/plan/usage-limits`
(`{limits: [{type, percentUsed, resetsAt}]}`, what app.cline.bot's
subscription page shows). An account without ClinePass (a 404 there) has
none; limits that fail to read for any other reason say so on the card beside
the balance, and limits read are kept when the balance can't be.

### DeepSeek models only through DeepSeek's own API

Cline's gateway picks among the providers that serve a model. With the
`pinUpstream` option on, a request for a DeepSeek model (`cline-pass/deepseek-…`,
not the `cline-free/` ones) carries `"providerOptions": {"gateway": {"only":
["deepseek"]}}`, so it is answered by DeepSeek's own API only, and one for a
GLM model (`cline-pass/glm-…`) carries `["zai"]`, so it is answered by Z.ai's
own API only — the same as magpie's built-in ClinePass tick. Other models, and a request with
`providerOptions` of its own, go as sent. It is off by default. Turn it on:

- in magpie: the provider's editor › Upstream › tick "DeepSeek and GLM
  models only from their makers' own APIs";
- in OpenCode: `"provider": {"cline": {"options": {"pinUpstream": true}}}` in
  `opencode.json`, or the plugin's own options:
  `"plugin": [["@magpie-community/opencode-cline-auth", {"pinUpstream": true}]]`.

## Models

The list is Cline's own, merged from the two feeds its clients read: the
recommended-models feed (its recommended picks, its free models and
ClinePass's) and the whole cloud catalog (`/ai/cline/models`, where the
usage-billed models the recommended feed doesn't name live). Refreshed from
the live feeds whenever they answer; until then a bundled snapshot of the
recommended list, Cline's own default (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) among it.
Cline's `clineCloud` group is left out, as Cline's own clients leave it out
unless they opt in.

Each model's context window is the cloud catalog's (`context_length`). Its
reply limit is left unsaid: the catalog's `max_completion_tokens` can be most
of the window, and an agent keeps that much free for the reply. The `cline-free/…`
and `cline-pass/…` models aren't in that catalog, so they say none, and magpie
takes the window models.dev gives the model after the prefix
(`cline-free/mimo-v2.6-flash` is `mimo-v2.6-flash`).

- The **free** group (`cline-free/…`, `stealth/…`) costs nothing — the names
  say "(free)". They are gated on the client surface a request claims; the
  plugin claims what it is, and the gate takes it. If Cline ever narrows that
  gate to its own apps, those models go away.
- The **ClinePass** group (`cline-pass/…`) needs a ClinePass subscription —
  the names say so, and asking without one answers 403.
- The rest are usage-billed against the account's Credits balance.

## Not included

- Cline's MCP and web-search endpoints — a chat provider only.
- Team/organization account switching.

# @magpie-community/opencode-commandcode-auth

Signs in to a [Command Code](https://commandcode.ai) plan (Pro, GOAT, Max,
Ultra, Go, Teams Pro) and makes its requests, in OpenCode and in magpie.
Provider id: `commandcode-plan`.

## Signing in

An account is a Command Code API key. There are three ways to get one:

- **Command Code (browser)**: the CLI's own sign-in. Studio asks you to
  approve a key for this machine, then posts it to a callback on
  `127.0.0.1`. The plugin checks the key with `/alpha/whoami` and reads the
  plan.
- **Command Code CLI's sign-in**: takes the account `commandcode login`
  signed in to, from `~/.commandcode/auth.json`. The file is only read,
  never changed.
- **API key**: paste a key from
  [commandcode.ai/settings/keys](https://commandcode.ai/settings/keys).

The key is kept where OpenCode keeps sign-ins (`auth.json`; in magpie,
`plugin-auth.json`) as `{ "type": "api", "key", "metadata": { "email": <user>, "plan" } }`.
Keys don't expire, so there is nothing to refresh.

## Requests

- **Every plan but Go** uses the Provider API at
  `https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1`. Every request carries the key
  as both `Authorization: Bearer` and `x-api-key`.
  - Claude models speak Anthropic's Messages API.
  - The other models speak chat completions.
- **Go** has no Provider API access. Its key is only accepted where the CLI
  asks, `POST /alpha/generate`, in the CLI's own format (command-code
  1.72.2 and its headers). The plugin's `fetch` handles this:
  - It turns OpenCode's chat completion into that format.
  - It turns the line-by-line reply back into a chat completion, streamed
    or not.
  - Failures keep their statuses: a model the plan lacks is a 403, running
    out of credits is a 402, and a usage-window limit is a 429.
  - A reply that stops before its finish line is a 502, unless it was
    streamed and had already said something. Then it ends cut short, with
    a note saying so, and `[DONE]` (#91).

The plan is read from `/alpha/billing/subscriptions`. It is cached for 10
minutes; after a failed read, the plugin tries again after 1 minute.
When the plan isn't known yet and the Provider API refuses the key with
"Your Go plan doesn't include API access", the key is taken as Go's from
then on (and saved so with it), and a chat completion is sent again to
`/alpha/generate`.

## Zero Data Retention

[Zero Data Retention](https://commandcode.ai/docs/resources/zdr) sends
requests only to upstreams that keep no prompts or replies. It is off
until you turn it on, either way:

- **In magpie**: turn on **Zero Data Retention** in the Command Code
  provider's editor (magpie v0.1.1231 or later). The switch is read at
  each request, so it needs no restart.
- **Anywhere** (OpenCode too): set `CMD_ZDR=1` in the environment of the
  process the plugin runs in, as for Command Code's CLI. Only `1` turns it
  on.

While it is on, every request for a reply carries `x-cmd-zdr: 1`, on the
Provider API and on Go's `/alpha/generate` alike, as the CLI sends it with `CMD_ZDR=1`.
ZDR requests usually cost more. A model with no ZDR upstream is refused,
and the refusal reaches the agent as Command Code said it: on the Provider
API a 422 with code `cmd_zdr_no_providers`, on Go a 400 whose type is
`cmd_zdr_no_providers`. Turn the switch off, or pick another model.

## Models

The `config` hook declares the default list:

| Model | Context window |
|---|---|
| Claude Sonnet 5 | 1M |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | 1M |
| GPT-6 Sol | 1.05M |
| DeepSeek V4 Pro | 1M |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash | 1M |
| Kimi K3 | 1M |
| GLM-5.3 | 1M |
| MiniMax M3 | 1M |

Once signed in, the `provider.models` hook replaces the default list with
the account's own:

Command Code's `/models` list is the same for every plan. A plan's list is
that list less the models the plan may not use, as the CLI's own table
(command-code 1.79.2) has it:

- **Go** and **GOAT** may not use the premium models (Claude Sonnet 5 and
  Opus, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, …). Go is also blocked from GOAT's own
  (Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.6 and 4.7, …).
- **Pro** may not use Claude Opus and Fable, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and
  Fugu Ultra; **Provider** may not use GPT-6.1 Sol.
- **Max**, **Ultra** and **Teams Pro** may use every model.

An account with bought or free credits may use every model, and so may one
whose plan can't be read: then the whole list is shown. A model the plan
doesn't have is still refused by Command Code (403 `MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN`), and
that refusal reaches the agent.

- **Every plan but Go**: the Provider API's `/models` list. Each model's
  `supported_endpoints` picks the API it speaks.
- **Go**: the same `/models` list, asked without the key (it answers
  without one, and Go's key has no Provider API). That is 56 models as of
  2026-10-13. When the list can't be had, the CLI's own Go table (57
  models) stands in.

  The Go models carry their reasoning levels, and a requested level is
  fitted to the nearest one the model has.

The `/models` list doesn't say which models take images. A model is marked
as taking them when it is a Claude model, or when the default list or the
CLI's table says so. For any other model the plugin says nothing either
way, and magpie answers from models.dev, as its built-in did.

## Not included

- Usage and quota (`/alpha/billing/credits`, the 5-hour and weekly windows).
- Switching between several accounts. OpenCode keeps one sign-in per
  provider.

# @magpie-community/opencode-cursor-auth

Signs in to a [Cursor](https://cursor.com) subscription (Pro, Pro+, Ultra,
Teams) and makes its requests on the API `cursor-agent` talks to, in
OpenCode and in magpie. Provider id: `cursor`.

## Signing in

An account is a Cursor access token. There are three ways to get one:

- **Cursor (browser)**: the sign-in `cursor-agent login` does. The page
  `cursor.com/loginDeepControl` is opened with a PKCE challenge, and the
  plugin polls `api2.cursor.sh/auth/poll` until the browser has signed in.
  The account is named by its email (`DashboardService/GetMe`).
- **cursor-agent's sign-in**: takes the account `cursor-agent login`
  signed in to. Its token is read from where the CLI keeps it: the macOS
  keychain (`cursor-access-token`), else its `auth.json` (`~/.cursor/`,
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cursor/` or `%APPDATA%\Cursor\`). A keychain read is
  kept for 10 seconds, and one the keychain refused (the user said no to
  its dialog) is not asked again for 10 minutes; signing in reads it
  afresh. The plugin never writes it; when it has less than 5 minutes
  left, `cursor-agent status` is run, which renews it.
- **Cursor API key**: a key from cursor.com/dashboard → Integrations. It is
  exchanged for a token at `/auth/exchange_user_api_key`, as the CLI does
  with `CURSOR_API_KEY`, and exchanged again when the token runs out.

Sign-ins are kept where OpenCode keeps them (`auth.json`; in magpie,
`plugin-auth.json`). A browser sign-in's token lasts about two months.
Cursor gives the CLI no way to renew it, so after that you sign in again.

## Requests

OpenCode speaks chat completions (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`); the
plugin's `fetch` answers them on Cursor's agent API:

- The agent API is the one `ServerConfigService/GetServerConfig` names for
  the account (a team may be served in one region only), else
  `agentn.global.api5.cursor.sh`. A refusal that names a region is tried
  once more with the config asked again.
- A fresh request opens `agent.v1.AgentService/Run`, a Connect stream both
  ways over HTTP/2, with the CLI's headers (`x-cursor-client-type: cli`,
  its version, privacy mode on).
- Where HTTP/2 can't open a Run (an error before its response, or none in
  15 s: a proxy or network that blocks HTTP/2), it goes as Cursor's clients
  run it without HTTP/2: `agent.v1.AgentService/RunSSE` down and a
  `aiserver.v1.BidiService/BidiAppend` for each client message up, over
  HTTP/1.1 on `api2.cursor.sh`, through the proxy magpie gives the request.
  When the failure says HTTP/2 itself can't be had (no head in 15 s,
  "h2 is not supported", no HTTP/2 in ALPN, a protocol error), the Runs
  after it go straight to HTTP/1.1 for 10 minutes; a failed connection
  (refused, no network) or a stream the server refused leaves the next Run
  to try HTTP/2 again. A region error over HTTP/1.1 sends the Run back to
  HTTP/2 at the region's agent host. A BidiAppend with no answer in 60 s
  (more for a large one) ends the Run, as cursor-agent does.
- A new Run imports the whole conversation as AI SDK messages kept as blobs
  the server asks for. The caller's tools are MCP tools, listed in the
  system prompt; the model calls them through Cursor's `CallDynamicTool`,
  and the calls come back as chat completion tool calls. Cursor's own tools
  (shell, file reads, edits) are never run.
- A conversation's Runs share one `conversation_id`, so Cursor sends them
  to the machine that has the prompt cached (Grok on Cursor caches by
  machine). It is made from what names the session — the request's
  `prompt_cache_key` (Codex's thread id), else the session the
  `chat.headers` hook is told — and the conversation's first user message,
  so subagents under one session are conversations of their own. With
  nothing naming the session, each Run has a new one.
- Text, thinking (`reasoning_content`) and token usage come back streamed
  or not. Replayed assistant `reasoning_content` (or `reasoning`) is kept as
  AI SDK reasoning parts in the next Run's transcript, including when a
  caller splits parallel tool calls across assistant messages. It stays
  separate from reply text; no thinking signature is invented.
  Cursor's `input_tokens` counts the cached prompt too: the cache
  read and written is taken out of it, and given as `cached_tokens` and
  `cache_write_tokens`, so it is counted once; its reasoning tokens are
  `reasoning_tokens`. A step that calls tools gets no usage in its Run
  (Cursor tells it only once the tools' results come back in the same
  Run), so once the Run is closed its usage is read from the dashboard's
  usage events, by the Run's conversation id: it shows in about 2.5 s,
  and is looked for up to 6 s. Far from Cursor it shows later than that
  (yetone/magpie#1053), so the step says 0 used and the conversation owes
  it: its next steps collect the event in the background, and a step
  that ends the turn waits for what is still owed, so the conversation
  adds up to what Cursor counted. What a step collected of earlier steps
  is not added to its own count, which a client reads as how full its
  context is: it is `usage.magpie_deferred` (`prompt_tokens`,
  `completion_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`), which
  magpie bills with the step and clients ignore. An account
  whose events miss the wait 3 steps in a row stops waiting for them.
  With nothing naming the session (so no later step to collect it), or
  an account that can't read its usage events, the step is estimated as
  before.
  Failures keep their statuses: 401 to sign in again, 429 at the
  usage limit, 400 for a prompt too long, 403 for a region refusal.

Tool results can continue a retained Run in the same plugin process. The owner
uses the same session/cache key and first user message as `conversation_id`, so
Task subagents sharing their parent's session can run independently. Retention
waits at most 120 seconds for a result batch and 15 minutes for a Run's total
lifetime. A continuation arriving in the last minute of that lifetime rebuilds
from supplied history before submitting results to the old Run. The absolute
deadline still applies to an active segment; it is never extended by activity.
The pool holds at most 8 owners per account and 32 per process, with
bounded history, blobs, arguments, and pending writes. When pending writes
reach their bound (a long history asks for its blobs at once, and a slow link
drains them slowly), the Run waits for the link to drain, and fails only if it
doesn't for 30 seconds.

A step's calls must all arrive within 30 seconds of each other: Cursor sends
each one once the model has written it, so a step of many long calls can take
longer than that in all (#155).

Cursor's count of a step's tool calls includes calls the plugin answers itself:
a tool the request doesn't have is refused to the model, and Cursor's own
`get_mcp_tools` is answered with the request's tools. The step's calls are the
rest.

These are retention limits. A missing, expired, restarted, busy, incompatible,
or full owner uses the original history reconstruction and stateless decoder
on a new Run. Pending parent calls and new input can take that path without
cancelling the parent's owner. Already supplied client tool results become
history; the plugin never executes those external tools. A failed native result
write is reported to that request because its outcome may be uncertain. A later
request can rebuild from its supplied history without submitting the result to
the old native exec again.

A native tool handoff reports zero usage with `magpie_native.accounting=pending`;
the final native answer bills the turn's totals. Its own `prompt_tokens` and
`completion_tokens` are its last model call's share (the larger of that
call's prompt estimate and the turn's mean per call), since a client reads
them as how full its context is; the earlier calls' share is
`usage.magpie_deferred` (#156). An identical completed retry
replays the saved response with zero usage. A native final also collects earlier
stateless debt as `usage.magpie_deferred`, separately from its own prompt total.
If a started native Run is abandoned after a pending handoff, its dashboard
count is owed once to the same account and conversation. Successful final
snapshots, including explicit zero, and cached replays do not enroll that debt.

Dashboard attribution uses event timestamps, rather than when events arrive.
Older debt is bounded strictly before the native Run's start, and keeps that
bound across later stateless Runs so an authoritative native event is not
billed again. An earlier event stamped on or after that boundary cannot be
identified reliably and stays unknown. Missing or ambiguous debt expires after
10 minutes; at most 64 distinct bounded debt groups are kept per account and
conversation, dropping the oldest on overflow. These counts are never guessed
as prior usage. Stateless Runs otherwise keep the dashboard accounting above.
`X-Magpie-Cursor-Continuity` identifies `same-run` or `stateless`, with the fallback
reason where available. A missing native batch count can retry stateless once
before any output is exposed or native result submitted; progressive output is
kept and its later errors are surfaced.

The existing request builder and model selection remain in use, including the
legacy `thinking=false` mapping for explicit `none`/`off`. Retention adds no
request-field whitelist or strict generation-option validation. Native tool
results preserve ordered text and data-URL images and explicit error flags;
unsupported native result shapes use the legacy history path.

## Models

The `config` hook declares `auto` (Cursor's pick). Once signed in, the
`provider.models` hook lists the account's models from Cursor's model
picker (`AiService/AvailableModels`, as the CLI asks for it, cached 10
minutes), the way pi-cursor-sdk lists Cursor's catalog:

- A model with a `context` parameter is listed once per size, as
  `<model>@<size>` named `<name> @ <size>` (`claude-opus-5-5@300k`,
  "Claude Opus 5.5 @ 300k"), its window that many tokens. A model with none
  is listed once, its window Cursor's `contextTokenLimit` (Max Mode's for a
  model served only in Max Mode); 200K when Cursor gives none.
- Effort is not a model of its own: the model's efforts are its variants,
  and the request's `reasoning_effort` (fitted to the nearest there is) is
  sent as the model's effort parameter. `none` turns a Claude's thinking off.
- Fast is not a model of its own either: a `service_tier` of `priority`
  or `fast` sends `fast=true`, anything else `fast=false` (it costs more,
  so only when asked). A model listed at a size Cursor has a fast variant
  of (served to the account) says `fast: true`, which magpie offers its
  Fast switch for (yetone/magpie#1360).
- A request goes as the picker's variant those parameters pick, in Max Mode
  when that variant is Max Mode's (a 1M size, say), as the CLI turns it on.
  A size with no variant goes in Max Mode when it is over Cursor's limit
  outside it. A model Cursor still answers "Max Mode Required" for is asked
  again in Max Mode, and so from then on.
- Hidden, Tab-only and chat-only models stay out, as in the CLI's picker.
- The usable list (`AgentService/GetUsableModels`, what `cursor-agent
  models` shows) says which variants the account has: a variant whose own
  id isn't in it is neither offered nor asked for (Sonnet 4.6 at any effort
  but medium, say), and a request for one goes as the nearest the account
  has. A model the usable list has nothing of is the picker's alone
  (GLM-5.3) and is kept whole; so is every model when Cursor can't give
  the usable list.
- An id from before 0.2.0 still runs. A variant's own id
  (`claude-opus-5-5-high`) is that variant; a family 0.1.x listed
  (`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-opus-5-5-fast`, `claude-haiku-5-5-thinking`,
  `cursor-grok-4.6`) is its variant nearest the default, fast for a `-fast`
  one; the picker's name for a model or a legacy slug of it is its default.
  Each is at the default context size, the request's `reasoning_effort`
  and `service_tier` counting as for a listed model. The list doesn't show
  these ids: pick the `@<size>` model for a window that is the model's.

## Usage

magpie shows Cursor Models, Other Models and Total for the billing period.
Accounts with a Grok Bot allowance also show its usage and reset time;
active trials are labelled separately. A spent Bot allowance doesn't stop
Cursor requests.

An account that may spend on-demand once its included usage is gone (a
team or personal spend limit, as `cursor-agent`'s usage view shows it) also
shows On-demand: its spend, and its limit when it has one. Cursor keeps
serving such an account past the included usage, so magpie doesn't count
it used up when Cursor Models or Other Models reach 100%; it does when the
on-demand spend reaches its limit. A team member with no limit of their
own spends the team's pool: On-demand shows the pool's spend and limit,
with the member's own spend beside it, and the account is used up when
the pool is.

Sign in to the Cursor account linked in Grok Bot. A linked SuperGrok
subscription grants Bot access without a paid Cursor plan; see
[Grok Bot plans and billing](https://cursor.com/help/grok-bot/plans).

## Not included

- Web search: Cursor's own web search is refused like its other tools.
- Switching between several accounts. OpenCode keeps one sign-in per
  provider.
- The Responses and Messages APIs: only chat completions are answered.

# @magpie-community/opencode-devin-auth

Signs in to a [Devin](https://devin.ai) subscription, the account the
`devin` CLI uses, and makes its requests, in OpenCode and in magpie.
Provider id: `devin`.

## Signing in

An account is the CLI's session token (`devin-session-token$…`). There are
two ways to get one:

- **Devin (browser)**: the CLI's own `devin auth login`, run by the
  plugin. It is a PKCE sign-in through `app.devin.ai/auth/cli/continue`
  back to a callback on `127.0.0.1`. The code is exchanged for the token
  at `server.codeium.com` (`ExchangeDevinCLIPKCECode`).
- **Devin CLI's sign-in**: takes the account the CLI is signed in to, from
  its `credentials.toml` (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/devin/`, by default
  `~/.local/share/devin/`; `%APPDATA%\devin\` on Windows). The file is only
  read, never changed.

The plugin names the account as Devin does when asked with the token
(`GetUserStatus`: its email and tier). When Devin can't tell, and the CLI
is installed, it asks `devin auth status`, run with a data folder of the
plugin's own, `~/.cache/opencode-devin-auth/<hash of the token>/`, so the
CLI's own sign-in is never touched. A CLI that reads another
`credentials.toml` than that folder's (on Windows it reads
`%APPDATA%\devin\` whatever it is run with) isn't asked: it would name
its own account. Otherwise the account is named "Devin".

The token is kept where OpenCode keeps sign-ins (`auth.json`; in magpie,
`plugin-auth.json`) as `{ "type": "api", "key", "metadata": { "email", "plan" } }`.
Devin doesn't expire it on a schedule, so there is nothing to refresh;
when it is refused, requests fail with a 401 saying to sign in again.

## Requests

Devin serves chat through Windsurf's API server, as the CLI does:
`POST https://server.codeium.com/exa.api_server_pb.ApiServerService/GetChatMessage`,
a Connect RPC in protobuf, with `Authorization: Basic <token>`.
`WINDSURF_API_SERVER_URL` moves the server, as it does for the CLI.

The plugin's `fetch` handles this:

- It turns OpenCode's chat completion into the CLI's request (devin-cli
  3000.11.3).
  - The system prompt goes at the head of the first user message.
  - Each tool's description goes there too, in a `<tool_descriptions>`
    block, and the tool is sent with a pointer to it. Devin answers "an
    internal error occurred" to some agents' tool descriptions when they
    are sent as the tools' own.
  - A tool call the conversation never answered is answered with "Tool use
    was interrupted and did not produce a result."
  - Images must be inline (`data:` URLs). The images a tool returned go
    with its result, as magpie's built-in sends them: a tool message's own
    `image_url` parts, and the ones magpie's gateway puts in the user
    message after the results ("[From the result of …]").
- It turns the streamed reply back into a chat completion, streamed or
  not: text, reasoning, tool calls and usage.
- Failures keep their statuses: a refused token is a 401, a usage limit a
  429, a prompt too long for the model a 400.

## Models

Devin's models are families: `swe-2`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `gpt-6-sol`, …
Each family has variants at each effort (`swe-2-high`,
`claude-opus-5-5-xhigh`), and some have a fast or priority run
(`claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`). The plugin lists each family once, with
the efforts its variants are at, plus its fast or priority run
(`claude-opus-5-5-fast`). The variant asked for is the one at the effort
picked, or the nearest the family has; with none picked, the family's
default. Variants at no effort (`glm-5-2-1m`) are listed as they are.
Adaptive and Fusion aren't listed; they route between models inside
Devin's own agent.

The `config` hook declares Devin's list as of 2026-10-14 (89 models).
Once signed in, the `provider.models` hook replaces it with the account's
own: what Devin tells the CLI's model picker for the account's token
(`GetCliModelConfigs`, the list `devin models list` prints), with or
without the CLI and on every system. When Devin can't be asked, the list
is the CLI's `devin models list`, if the CLI names the account Devin names
the token's (on Windows it reads its own sign-in whatever folder it is
given, so it answers only for that account); else the declared list. The
list is cached for 5 minutes; after a failed read, the plugin tries again
after 1 minute.

Which models take images is what Devin tells its CLI's model picker
(`GetCliModelConfigs`, each model's `supports_images`), asked once signed
in, with or without the CLI, and cached as the list is: `swe-2`, `swe-1.7`
and most others do; GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, Inkling, Nemotron, DeepSeek V4 Flash
and V4 Pro don't. Before Devin is asked, or when it can't be, the declared
list says what Devin said on 2026-10-05. A model Devin says nothing of
takes models.dev's word.

## Not included

magpie's built-in Devin account does more than this plugin:

- **Usage**: the plan's quota windows.
- **Several accounts** at once.
- **Web search**: its stand-in for Anthropic's server-side web search tool.
